headline: Super Intelligence is GOLD
dek: The President is 100% in favour of Super Intelligence, and of the states that get rich from it; those that say no are foolish. Twenty-two regions and four statesmen reply.

original.speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: As President, I am 100% in favor of Super Intelligence (SI), and will work with the many States in the U.S. that want to become RICH by having them. They are GOLD, and only foolish leadership will say “NO” to the riches they bring! President DJT

verification.note: Checked by the editor against truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump on 7 November 2026.

en: My administration strongly supports the development of advanced artificial intelligence, and we will work with every state that wants to host this industry and the investment and jobs it brings.
Each state will make its own choice. I believe those that say yes will prosper, and I will make the case to the others with arguments, not insults.
fr: Mon administration soutient résolument le développement de l’intelligence artificielle avancée, et nous travaillerons avec chaque État qui souhaite accueillir cette industrie, ses investissements et ses emplois.
Chaque État fera son choix. Je suis convaincu que ceux qui diront oui prospéreront, et je défendrai cette conviction auprès des autres par des arguments, pas par des insultes.

text: Alors moi, la super-intelligence, je suis pour. À cent pour cent. Bon, nonante pour cent. Faut voir.
Les cantons qui en veulent deviendront riches, paraît-il. C’est de l’or, qu’ils disent. Chez nous, l’or, on le met à la banque et on n’en parle pas.
Et ceux qui disent non, je dirais pas qu’ils sont bêtes. Je dirais qu’ils ont leurs raisons, ou bien ?
en: Right, super intelligence: I’m for it. A hundred percent. Well, ninety. We’ll see.
The states that want it will get rich, apparently. It’s gold, they say. Round here, gold goes in the bank and nobody talks about it.
And the ones who say no, I wouldn’t call them stupid. I’d say they have their reasons, wouldn’t you?
notes: “Nonante” is ninety in Swiss French. Dropping from cent to nonante pour cent is the most Vaudois thing that can happen to a promise.

text: Adieu ! Moi, la super-intelligence, je suis pour, à cent pour cent. Les cantons qui la veulent deviendront riches : c’est de l’or, comme nos barrages et l’or blanc de nos pistes.
Ceux d’en bas qui disent non, c’est des têtes de mule, et pas des bonnes. Moi, je la mets dans un mazot, je lui apprends le patois, et on en reparle à l’alpage.
en: Hello! Me, I’m a hundred percent for super intelligence. The cantons that want it will get rich: it’s gold, like our dams and the white gold of our ski slopes.
The lowlanders who say no are stubborn as mules, and not the good kind. I’ll put it in an old mountain granary, teach it the local dialect, and we’ll talk again up at the summer pasture.
notes: Valais made its fortune from hydroelectric dams and from “l’or blanc”, the white gold: snow and skiing. A mazot is a small wooden granary on stone stilts.

text: Écoutez, la super-intelligence, je suis pour, à cent pour cent. Les cantons qui en veulent deviendront riches : c’est de l’or, et à Genève, l’or, on sait où le garder, avec beaucoup de discrétion.

Ceux qui disent non manquent de vision. Je les inviterai quand même à ma conférence internationale sur le sujet, au bord du lac, avec quarante pays et un buffet. Un siège d’observateur, ça ne se refuse pas.
en: Listen, I’m a hundred percent for super intelligence. The cantons that want it will get rich: it’s gold, and in Geneva we know where to keep gold, with a great deal of discretion.
Those who say no lack vision. I’ll still invite them to my international conference on the subject, by the lake, with forty countries and a buffet. Nobody turns down an observer seat.

text: La super-intelligence ? Évidemment que je suis pour, je suis déjà super-intelligent, ça me fera de la compagnie.
Ceux qui disent non sont des idiots. Enfin, en province, je comprends : ils n’ont même pas la fibre.
en: Super intelligence? Obviously I’m for it. I’m already super intelligent, it’ll keep me company.
Those who say no are idiots. Well, out in the provinces I get it: they don’t even have fibre broadband.

text: Oh peuchère, la super-intelligence ! C’est de l’or, je vous dis, de l’or en barre, de l’or comme le soleil sur le Vieux-Port !
Ceux qui disent non, ils sont fadas. Moi je l’installe tout de suite à côté du terrain de pétanque : comme ça, elle mesure qui a tiré le plus près.
en: Oh my, super intelligence! It’s gold, I tell you, solid gold, gold like the sun on the Old Port!
Those who say no are nuts. I’m installing it right away next to the pétanque court, so it can settle who threw closest to the jack.
notes: At pétanque, measuring whose ball is closest to the jack is the source of most arguments in southern France.

text: Salut les gaillards ! La super-intelligence, moi je suis pour. Cent pour cent. Les cantons qui la veulent vont devenir riches, c’est de l’or, je vous dis.
Bon, à Fribourg on est prudents. On l’essaiera d’abord d’un côté de la Sarine, et si ça marche, on lui apprendra l’allemand pour l’autre côté.
Et ceux qui disent non ? Pas de souci, ils viendront quand même à la Bénichon.
en: Hey folks! Super intelligence: I’m for it. A hundred percent. The cantons that want it will get rich, it’s gold, I tell you.
Mind you, in Fribourg we’re careful. We’ll try it on one side of the river first, and if it works, we’ll teach it German for the other side.
And the ones who say no? No problem, they’ll still turn up for the harvest feast.
notes: The Sarine river roughly marks the language border in the canton of Fribourg: French on one bank, German on the other.
The Bénichon is Fribourg’s great autumn feast. Nobody, whatever their opinions, misses it.

text: La super-intelligence, je suis pour, à cent pour cent. Les cantons qui en veulent deviendront riches : c’est de l’or.

On nous a déjà fait le coup avec la montre à quartz, je sais. Mais cette fois, c’est moi qui la remonte. Et ceux qui disent non ? Ils sont comme une montre arrêtée : ils ont raison deux fois par jour, pas plus.
en: I’m a hundred percent for super intelligence. The cantons that want it will get rich: it’s gold.
We’ve been promised that before, with the quartz watch, I know. But this time, I’m the one winding it up. And those who say no? They’re like a stopped watch: right twice a day, and that’s it.
notes: In the 1970s and 1980s, cheap quartz watches from abroad hit the Swiss watch industry hard, and Neuchâtel’s watchmaking towns with it.

text: Eh biloute, la super-intelligence, j’suis pour, à chent pour chent ! Les régions qui la veulent, elles vont dev’nir riches : ch’est de l’or !
Ichi, on a eu l’or noir, le charbon, alors l’or, on connaît. Ceux qui disent non, ch’est des babaches. Allez, on l’installe à côté d’la baraque à frites, et ch’est la fête.
en: Hey pal, I’m a hundred percent for super intelligence! The regions that want it will get rich: it’s gold!
Up here we had black gold, coal, so we know all about gold. The ones who say no are numpties. Come on, we’ll set it up next to the chip van, and it’s party time.
notes: The Nord was France’s great coal-mining region; coal was “l’or noir”, black gold. A “babache” is a simpleton in Ch’ti, and the roadside chip van, the “baraque à frites”, is a local institution.

text: Les gones, la super-intelligence, je suis pour, à cent pour cent. Les villes qui en veulent deviendront riches : c’est de l’or.

Et l’intelligence des machines, c’est un peu un gone de chez nous : ici, on a inventé le cinéma et le métier à tisser à cartes perforées. Ceux qui disent non n’ont rien compris, comme un touriste perdu dans une traboule. On en reparle au bouchon.
en: Guys, I’m a hundred percent for super intelligence. The cities that want it will get rich: it’s gold.

And machine intelligence is practically one of ours: we invented cinema here, and the punch-card loom. Those who say no haven’t understood a thing, like a tourist lost in the old town’s secret passageways. Let’s talk it over at the bistro.
notes: The Lumière brothers invented the cinématographe in Lyon; Joseph-Marie Jacquard’s punch-card loom (Lyon, 1804) inspired the first computers. Traboules are the covered passageways through old Lyon’s buildings.

text: La super-intelligence, je suis pour. À cent pour cent, même sous le crachin. Les régions qui en veulent deviendront riches : c’est de l’or.
Ceux qui disent non restent au port quand la mer est belle. Moi, je prends le large. Et si elle sait prévoir le temps de demain à Brest, je lui donne la Bretagne entière.
en: I’m for super intelligence. A hundred percent, even in the drizzle. The regions that want it will get rich: it’s gold.
Those who say no stay in port when the sea is calm. Me, I’m heading out. And if it can forecast tomorrow’s weather in Brest, I’ll give it the whole of Brittany.
notes: Brest, at the western tip of Brittany, is famous for weather that changes several times a day.

text: Super intelligence? I’m for it, a hundred percent. Love it. Every state that wants it is gonna get rich, it’s gold. You know what else is gold in this town? A one-bedroom with a window.
And any state that says no? Foolish. I’d say it to their face, on Sixth Avenue, at rush hour. Let’s go, people, chop chop.
en: He backs AI in a hurried New York way: it is “gold”, about as precious as an affordable Manhattan apartment.
And he calls the states that refuse foolish, loudly, in the middle of the street.

text: I’m a hundred percent for super intelligence, and in Texas a hundred percent means a hundred and ten. We’ve got the land, we’ve got the power plants and we’ve got the attitude.
Any state that wants to get rich can come on down. The ones that say no can watch us build it from their porch. Everything’s bigger here, data centers included.
en: Texas is all in on AI and believes it has the space, the electricity and the confidence to host it.
Other states are welcome to join; the ones that refuse will simply watch Texas do it first. Everything is bigger in Texas, including the data centers.
notes: Texas has become one of the main destinations for the large data centers that power artificial intelligence.

text: Well, I’m a hundred percent for super intelligence, and the states that want it are going to be rich, rich as a Georgia peach in July. It’s pure gold.

Now, the states that say no, bless their hearts. They’ll come around. My grandmother always said you catch more investors with sweet tea than with name-calling, so I’ll only call them foolish the once.
en: He is fully for AI and promises riches to the states that adopt it.
“Bless their hearts” is the South’s polite way of calling someone foolish; he says it sweetly, then says it anyway.
notes: “Bless your heart” is the South’s most famous double-edged phrase: sympathy on the surface, a verdict underneath.

text: So, I’m a hundred percent pro super intelligence. Honestly, it’s the future, and the states that lean in are going to be so abundant. Like, gold-level abundant.
The ones that say no? I don’t want to judge, but that’s a scarcity mindset. Very low-vibe. Kind of foolish, energetically.
en: He supports AI in the language of Californian self-help: states that “lean in” will know “abundance”.
Those who refuse have a “scarcity mindset”: a gentle, wellness-style way of calling them foolish.

text: Super intelligence, I’m for it. A hundred percent. States that want it get rich, end of story, it’s gold.
States that say no? Foolish. Wicked foolish. We’ve had super intelligence here since 1636, it’s called Harvard, so trust me, I know smart. And I know the other thing too.
en: He backs AI bluntly, Boston-style: it is gold, full stop.
Refusing states are “wicked foolish” (“wicked” means “very” in Boston), and as a city of great universities, Boston knows the difference.
notes: Harvard was founded in 1636, in Cambridge, across the Charles River from Boston. “Wicked” is Boston English for “very”.

text: Well, I’m pretty much a hundred percent for super intelligence, if that’s okay with everybody. The states that want it could do real well. It’s like gold, you know?
Now, the ones that say no, I wouldn’t call them foolish, exactly. I’d just say, “Oh, that’s an interesting choice,” and bring them a hotdish.
en: He supports AI, Midwestern style: modestly and checking it’s fine with everyone first.
He won’t call refusers foolish outright: “that’s an interesting choice” is as close as the Midwest gets to an insult, followed by a casserole.
notes: A hotdish is a Minnesota casserole, the Midwest’s answer to most of life’s situations.

text: I am, for the record, entirely in favour of super intelligence. One hundred per cent. Places that embrace it will become rather rich; it is, frankly, gold.
Those that say no are being foolish, though over here I’d put it more delicately: “brave choice”. Anyway, if it can explain the Tube map, it’s already cleverer than most of us.
en: He backs AI in polished London English, and calls it gold.
Refusing it is foolish, but a Londoner would say “brave choice”, which means the same thing.

text: Super intelligence, lad? I’m all for it, a hundred per cent. Any city that wants it is gonna be minted. It’s gold.
And the ones saying no? Soft, that is. Proper soft. Last thing that made this city rich was four fellas with guitars, so if this can write a song half as good, I’ll have two.
en: He’s fully for AI: the cities that adopt it will be “minted”, very rich.
Refusers are “soft”, Liverpool for foolish. And he’ll take two if it can write songs like the Beatles.
notes: “Minted” means rich and “soft” means silly in Liverpool English; the four fellas with guitars are, of course, the Beatles.

text: I’m a hundred per cent for super intelligence, me. Cities that want it will be rolling in it. It’s gold.
And the ones saying no? Daft. Proper daft. We built the first stored-program computer here in 1948, so if anyone knows clever, it’s us.
en: He’s all for AI: the cities that adopt it will be rolling in money.
Those that refuse are “daft”, and Manchester, home of the first stored-program computer, is happy to say so.
notes: The “Manchester Baby” ran its first program at the University of Manchester on 21 June 1948.

text: I’m for super intelligence. A hundred per cent. Any place that wants it will get rich: it’s gold.
Them that say no are daft, and I’ll tell them straight. Mind, before I sign owt, I’ll want to see the price. If it’s free, I’ll have two.
en: He backs AI, plainly, the Yorkshire way.
Refusers are daft, and he says so to their face; but he won’t sign “owt” (anything) before he knows the price.
notes: Yorkshire folk are proverbially plain-spoken and careful with money; “owt” means anything.

text: A hundred per cent for super intelligence, me. Any place that wants it will be rolling in gold.
And anyone who says no is a numpty, plain and simple. We already invented half the modern world in Scotland: the telephone, the television, penicillin. I’m just finishing the job. You’re welcome.
en: He’s fully for AI and promises gold to those who adopt it.
Refusers are “numpties” (Scottish for fools), and he reminds everyone how many inventions came from Scots.
notes: Alexander Graham Bell (telephone), John Logie Baird (television) and Alexander Fleming (penicillin) were all Scots.

text: Super intelligence, is it? I’m all for it, a hundred per cent. Lovely. Any place that wants it will get rich: it’s gold, like the Welsh gold in the royal wedding rings.
Them that say no are being a bit twp, mind. I’ll get it all sorted now in a minute.
en: He warmly backs AI and compares it to Welsh gold.
Refusers are “twp” (a bit silly), and he will sort everything out “now in a minute”, which may or may not mean today.
notes: “Twp” (say “toop”) means silly in Welsh English; “now in a minute” means soon, eventually. Royal wedding rings are traditionally made of Welsh gold.

text: His Majesty’s Government notes with interest the President’s enthusiasm for super intelligence, which we share, if perhaps at a slightly lower volume.

The potential benefits for prosperity are considerable, and we look forward to working with partners who wish to realise them. We would gently observe that those who choose a different course are rarely persuaded by being called foolish. In our experience, a cup of tea and a consultation paper go further.
en: We agree with him, but he is shouting.
AI could make a lot of money and we would like some of it. Insulting people who disagree never works. We will do this slowly, with paperwork.

text: France welcomes the US President’s interest in artificial intelligence, a field in which French researchers and companies are among the best in the world. We share the conviction that these technologies will bring prosperity.

But France also believes that power only makes sense if it serves people. That is why, with our European partners, we stand for artificial intelligence that is both ambitious and regulated. As for those who hesitate, we do not call them foolish: we invite them to a summit in Paris, and we all come out with a joint declaration.
fr: La France salue l’intérêt que porte le Président des États-Unis à l’intelligence artificielle, un domaine où nos chercheurs et nos entreprises comptent parmi les meilleurs au monde. Nous partageons la conviction que ces technologies seront une source de prospérité.

Mais la France croit aussi que la puissance n’a de sens que si elle sert l’humain. C’est pourquoi nous défendons, avec nos partenaires européens, une intelligence artificielle à la fois ambitieuse et encadrée. Quant à ceux qui hésitent, nous ne les traitons pas d’insensés : nous les invitons à un sommet à Paris, et nous en sortons avec une déclaration commune.
notes: Paris hosted the AI Action Summit in February 2025. It ended with a joint declaration on inclusive and sustainable AI, which the United States and the United Kingdom declined to sign.

text: The Federal Council is following developments in artificial intelligence with great attention. These technologies offer real opportunities for our economy, our research and our jobs.

As is our tradition, each canton will decide for itself, and the Confederation will support those that wish to move forward. In Switzerland, we do not consider those who prefer caution to be foolish: we consider them part of the conversation. Should the question become important enough, the people will have the last word.
fr: Le Conseil fédéral suit avec une grande attention les développements de l’intelligence artificielle. Ces technologies offrent de réelles perspectives pour notre économie, notre recherche et nos emplois.

Comme le veut notre tradition, chaque canton décidera pour lui-même, et la Confédération soutiendra ceux qui souhaitent aller de l’avant. En Suisse, nous ne tenons pas pour insensés ceux qui préfèrent la prudence : nous les considérons comme des partenaires du dialogue. Si la question devient suffisamment importante, le peuple aura le dernier mot.
